implementation_statement: The owner is the only administrator of every SaaS account and creates student portal accounts when a family enrolls. Gaps: the former web designer's collaborator account on the website builder was still active (found 2026-07-16 and removed that day); 27 portal accounts of students who stopped tutoring were still open; family members use the laptop under the owner's user account; no periodic account review.
evidence: Website-builder member and collaborator lists; laptop user accounts (P07)

implementation_statement: The client-management SaaS separates the owner's administrator view from each parent's view of their own invoices and schedule. The website builder's members area shows each student only their own assignments, uploads, and messages.
evidence: Vendor role settings; client-management SaaS SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-tutor holds every role and there is no bookkeeper. Card payments run through the processor's hosted page in SYS-02, so the owner never handles card numbers, and the tax preparer (CPA firm) receives the annual accounting export. The IT technician has no standing access. Gap: no one else approves account or setting changes.
evidence: SYS-02 payment settings; annual accounting export

implementation_statement: The phone locks after 1 minute with a passcode or biometric. Gap: the laptop locked only after 15 minutes idle and is often left open in the family room; set to 5 minutes by 2026-08-14.

The owner has had no security or children's privacy training. By 2026-10-31 the owner completes a free online security basics course for small businesses, reads the FTC's COPPA compliance guidance, and subscribes to monthly security reminders.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The email suite, website builder, client-management SaaS, and video platform each keep a sign-in history. Nobody has ever reviewed one. From 2026-09 the owner reviews them on the first Monday of each month and notes the review in the security log.

provider_if_inherited: Email suite vendor; website-builder vendor; video platform vendor; client-management SaaS vendor
implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the logs stay with the vendors. The email suite, website builder, video platform, and client-management SaaS each keep their sign-in history on the vendor's platform, not on the shared laptop.
evidence: Vendor sign-in history screens; client-management SaaS SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the P07 plan states openly that independence is limited, because the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls with help from the on-call IT technician. POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the business, such as the IT technician, at least every second year. The client-management SaaS vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report, reviewed in P09, covers the vendor's inherited controls. Gap: the first outside review has not taken place.

Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the owner is the change control element. POL-01 4.3 requires a risk assessment update after a new system, vendor, or portal feature. POL-01 5.3 bars collecting any new kind of information from children until every affected parent has received a new direct notice and consented. Gap: POL-01 has no change log for account or portal settings.

The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gaps: the sealed emergency sheet with recovery codes and the backup-tutor agreement are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).

provider_if_inherited: Client-management SaaS vendor; email and files suite vendor
implementation_statement: The client-management SaaS vendor backs up schedules, notes, and invoices (inherited; stated in its SOC 2 report). Owner responsibility: student folders exist only in cloud storage with desktop sync and 30-day version history, so ransomware on the laptop would sync encrypted copies. A restore of one folder from version history worked on 2026-07-16. No backup independent of sync.

The owner signs in to each SaaS with a personal named account; each student has an individual portal account. Gaps: family members use the laptop under the owner's user account, and the owner sets student portal passwords and keeps them in a spreadsheet in the email suite.
evidence: Laptop user list; portal member list

provider_if_inherited: Client-management SaaS vendor; email and files suite vendor; website-builder vendor; video platform vendor
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced on the client-management SaaS administrator account. Gap: the email suite administrator, website-builder administrator, and video platform account sign in with a password only. All three offer MFA at no cost; the owner turns it on by 2026-08-14 and saves recovery codes.
evidence: Account security pages; sign-in tests on 2026-07-16 (P07)

provider_if_inherited: Accounting SaaS vendor; email and files suite vendor
implementation_statement: MFA is on for the accounting SaaS. Gap: the owner's everyday email and files mailbox has no MFA (the owner's only email account is also the suite administrator).

Passwords are saved in the browser; two are reused across accounts. Student portal passwords are set by the owner and listed in a spreadsheet. A password manager and parent-set portal passwords replace both by 2026-08-14; the spreadsheet is deleted.
The ransomware runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-07-31 with a contact list. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the plan not yet walked through (due 2026-09-30).

Paper worksheets and printed notes are shredded with a cross-cut shredder at home. Gap: no procedure for wiping old laptops and phones; the previous laptop (replaced 2024) is in a drawer with student files on it.

POL-01 section 9 (adopted 2026-07-31) sets the rules for business devices, including no family use. Gap: family members still use the laptop until the owner sets up a separate family device or account (due 2026-08-14).

Each parent e-signs an enrollment agreement in the client-management SaaS, with a photo and recording permission checkbox, and pays by card before the child gets a portal account. Gaps: the agreement does not say what the portal collects, how it is used, or who receives it, so the consent is not informed (16 CFR 312.4(c)(1)); reading-aloud audio was added in August 2025 without new consent; student information was given to a consumer AI assistant without any parent consent (P10).

No online notice of children's information practices exists on the website or the portal. A notice that meets 16 CFR 312.4(d), including the retention policy (312.10), is drafted for posting by 2026-08-14, before the fall term.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-17 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Repeated every July and after major changes, as 16 CFR 312.8(b)(2) requires at least annually.

The client-management SaaS vendor provides a SOC 2 Type 2 report and a data processing addendum; the IT technician signed a confidentiality and data-handling agreement on 2026-07-08. Gaps: no written security assurances reviewed for the website builder, video platform, or AI assistant; the AI assistant's consumer terms allow use of prompts to improve its models.

The router's built-in firewall and the laptop's host firewall are on. Gaps: the router admin password is still the default, and family and smart-home devices share one network. New admin password and a separate guest network for smart-home devices by 2026-08-14.
Every SaaS uses TLS (inherited). Gap: the owner texts parents about progress by ordinary SMS from the personal phone. Progress messages move to the client-management SaaS messaging by 2026-08-31.

The SaaS vendors encrypt stored data (inherited; stated for the client-management SaaS in its SOC 2 report). The phone is encrypted by its passcode. Gap: the laptop has no full-disk encryption; the owner turns on the built-in encryption by 2026-08-14.

provider_if_inherited: SaaS vendors; device operating system vendors
implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors patch their services. Automatic operating system and browser updates are on for the laptop and phone; the owner restarts when prompted. The router updates its firmware automatically.
The operating system's built-in antivirus runs real-time scanning with automatic updates on the laptop. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.

No retention policy existed: files on about 210 former students since 2019, 27 inactive portal accounts, and all session recordings are kept indefinitely. POL-01 section 8 sets a written retention schedule (16 CFR 312.10); the first purge is due 2026-09-30.
evidence: POL-01 Appendix A; file and portal review 2026-07-15
